newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt March 1997 tourism receipts up 21 pct-paper.
newsitem.headline: Egypt March 1997 tourism receipts up 21 pct-paper.

text.p: German tourists spent more time than any other visitors to Egypt during March and helped raise revenues for the month by 21 percent compared to March 1996, the tourism minister said in remarks published on Monday.
Tourism Minister Mamdouh el-Beltagi told the official Al-Ahram newspaper that revenues for March were $328.6 million, up from $271 million in March 1996.
Income from tourism, one of Egypt's main sources of hard currency, was $317 million in February 1997.
Beltagi said that the average length of time a tourist spent in Egypt during March also rose to 7.3 nights from 6.5 nights in the same month of 1996.
Germans were the longest staying visitors with a total of 228,000 nights and Italians came next with 84,000 nights, he added. Japanese, Swiss and Israelis stayed for the shortest periods of time.

In March 1996, Moslem militant gunmen shot dead 18 Greek tourists outside a Cairo hotel but the incident had little effect on the industry in subsequent months. Militant activity, which began in 1992, hit tourism receipts hard in 1993 and 1994.

Revenues from the tourism industry, the Suez Canal, visible exports and remittances from expatriate workers are the country's main sources of foreign currency. Egypt said it had earned a record $3 billion from tourism in the financial year 1995/6, which began on July 1, 1995.
